title: Magnetic Field and Properties of Materials — Quick Quiz

questions.q: What is the trajectory of a charged particle entering a uniform magnetic field at an angle θ = 90°?
questions.explanation: When θ = 90°, magnetic force acts as a purely centripetal force perpendicular to velocity, producing a circular orbit.

questions.q: The SI unit of Magnetic Flux Density (B) is:
questions.explanation: Tesla (T) is the SI unit of magnetic field density, where 1 T = 1 Wb/m².

questions.q: To convert a galvanometer into an ammeter, one must connect:
questions.explanation: Connecting a low resistance shunt S in parallel bypasses excess current around the delicate galvanometer coil.

questions.q: What is the magnetic field strength inside a toroid's central empty space?
questions.explanation: By Ampere's Law, no net current is enclosed by an Amperian loop inside the central hole, so B = 0.

questions.q: Two parallel wires carrying currents in opposite directions will:
questions.explanation: Anti-parallel currents produce repulsive magnetic forces by Fleming's Left-Hand Rule.

questions.q: Which rule determines the direction of magnetic force on a moving positive charge?
questions.explanation: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule gives the force vector direction on moving charges/conductors.

questions.q: The expression for Hall Voltage V_H across a sample of thickness t is:
options: V_H = B I n t / q
questions.explanation: Derivation yields V_H = B I / (n t q).

questions.q: Work done by a magnetic field on a moving charged particle is always:
questions.explanation: Since magnetic force is perpendicular to displacement (v·F = 0), work done is identically zero.

questions.q: Soft iron core in a Moving Coil Galvanometer is used to:
options: Produce a radial and strong magnetic field
questions.explanation: Soft iron core concentrates magnetic field lines, making the field radial and strongly enhancing sensitivity.

questions.q: Two parallel conductors carrying currents 1 A each separated by 1 m in vacuum experience a force per unit length of:
questions.explanation: By definition of 1 Ampere: f = μ₀ I₁ I₂ / (2π d) = (4π × 10⁻⁷ × 1 × 1)/(2π × 1) = 2 × 10⁻⁷ N/m.
